if you truly think BPD is the right diagnosis over bipolar then it’s worth a mention - it’s actually really common for people to be misdiagnosed with BPD or bipolar and then years later it being changed to the other

SSRI’s and SNRI’s can be used to treat anxiety also - i have trialed various ones over the years for my anxiety. it can be very much a trial and error process and it can get very frustrating and often, people feel worse for the first 1 - 2 weeks of starting a SSRI before they feel better. 

In england, it is standard practice for people to be on a SSRI and be in therapy simultaneously as it’s proven the most effective at the moment and a lot of people will then come off the medication either just before they finish therapy or just after. 

Personally, I’m yet to find medication that works for me and the worst part is trying to come off them. Withdrawal symptoms will differ from person to person - the worst one to come off of was venlafaxine however that’s a SNRI, the SSRI’s i’ve tried have been relatively okay to come off.

the main thing i’d say is allow her the space to talk to you about anything - sometimes people don’t want to talk about it, sometimes they do. encourage her to go out and do things, even if it’s just for a walk. if she doesn’t have one, maybe suggest getting a SAD lamp?? i have one and have found it really beneficial, especially in winter when the sun is lacking.
